_doc: Writing-form registry (spec 47 §8). The gate skeleton (identity/rubric/reader-testing/render-verify/self-improve) is form-agnostic and shared. Only length, exit platforms, and monetization change per form. A topic card's optional `form:` field selects one; absent = article. Never fabricate an exit that isn't wired: `exit_status` says what actually works today.

xpost.label: X post (short hook)

length.guidance: one finding, one hook; no hamburger template; lead IS the whole post

xpost.gate_notes: rubric axes lead/title_jargon/why_pay apply; jargon_defined relaxed (no room to define — pick a hook that needs no jargon); reader-testing = would a stranger scrolling get it in 3 seconds

article.label: Article (current default)

length.guidance: hamburger template, beginner-friendly, jargon defined on first use

article.monetization: note single-purchase ¥1000 + Substack paid $8/mo + free-tier reach
article.gate_notes: full gate skeleton, all axes apply

ebook.label: Ebook (long form)

length.guidance: multi-chapter, each chapter passes the article gate skeleton independently, one spine across chapters

exit_status.zenn-book: pending (zenn book format not yet wired)
exit_status.kdp: pending (Amazon KDP publisher not yet built)

ebook.monetization: ebook one-off sales (zenn book paid / KDP royalties)
ebook.gate_notes: run gate skeleton per chapter; title_jargon applies to book title AND chapter titles
